result.report:
I've planned the icon set as one module, ICONS, with two milestones. A builder can start once the design review passes. **That design review is still owed:** I couldn't start one from here, so the lead needs to run `agent_loop.py review --module ICONS --milestone design --worktree .`.

**Milestones**
- **M1, pick a look:** a builder draws the sun and high tide in three different hand-drawn styles, and you choose one. Suggested styles are a fine-liner, a two-pass pencil sketch and a loose dip pen. They go on `directions/index.html` at 24 and 48 px on light and dark. Your pick becomes the reference for the rest of the set, because one sitting choosing beats rejecting eight finished icons.
- **M2, the set and preview page:** all eight icons in the style you picked, plus `preview.html`. A reviewer then judges by eye:
  - each icon is recognisable at 24 px on a standard (non-retina) screen;
  - high and low tide read as a pair and can't be mistaken for wind or fog;
  - the lines look hand-inked, not jittery;
  - all eight look drawn by the same hand;
  - nothing is clipped at the edges.

**How the wobble is made (decided in the design)**
- The wobble is in the path shapes themselves, drawn with curves only. There are no filters, perfect circles or rectangles, or dashed lines.
- Wobble is gentle and scales with the length of each stroke.
- The preview page puts each icon's SVG code directly in the page. That's the only way `currentColor` picks up the dark-panel colour, and it's how the app will use them too.
- I built a quick test sun this way: it came to 720 bytes and showed correctly on light and dark in headless Chrome. The two-pass pencil style roughly doubles that, so it may come close to 1.5 kB on busier icons like rain.

**Automatic checks:** I wrote `tools/check_icons.py`, so builders aren't graded by checks they wrote themselves. It checks the 24×24 grid, stroke-only `currentColor`, file size, curves only, no `id`s, the same stroke settings across a set, and that the preview page contains every icon at each size and background. I tested it on good and bad samples. All milestone checks currently fail as expected, with no broken commands, and the overall project check passes on the empty repo.

**What you need to do**
1. **Pick the style when M1 finishes.** Open `directions/index.html` and record your choice with `agent_loop.py owner answer --module ICONS --milestone M1 --item M1.5 --worktree . --text '<your pick>'`.
2. **Integration is local only.** Builders update your local `main` and never push, because you haven't given permission to push. Changing that is your call.
3. **Assumptions** (all in the plan's log; overturn any in a line):
   - "Under 1.5kb" means under 1500 bytes on disk, not 1536.
   - The icons sit in a 24×24 box with about a unit of padding.
   - Stroke-only also rules out filters, a second colour made with opacity, and dashed lines.
   - File names are `sun`, `cloud`, `rain`, `wind`, `fog`, `high-tide`, `low-tide` and `moon`.
   - The moon is a single crescent, not a set of phases.
   - Light and dark are shown side by side on one page, not as a toggle.
   - M1 uses the sun and high tide as the sample icons.

Sources:
- [DEV: 1,756 hand-drawn icons and nobody drew them](https://dev.to/fantomiald/1756-hand-drawn-icons-and-nobody-drew-them-1cpi)
- [Rough.js docs (seed, roughness, bowing)](https://jsr.io/@rough/roughjs/doc)
- [wired-icon](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/wired-elements@3.0.0-rc.6/experimental/wired-icon/README.md)

PLANNED: ORCHESTRATE.md, docs/modules/ICONS.md, docs/modules/ICONS-PLAN.md, docs/modules/ICONS-DONE.json, tools/check_icons.py

**What changed**
- **Finding 1 (the contract check let bad SVGs through):** this was a real bug in `tools/check_icons.py`, so I fixed the checker and logged it, as the profile requires. Every icon's root `<svg>` must now set width and height 24, `fill="none"`, `stroke="currentColor"`, a positive `stroke-width`, and round line caps and joins. No child element may repeat any of these. Each folder must still use one `stroke-width`. Opacity attributes are now rejected too, which the plan's "stroke only" assumption already said. The reviewer's test SVG now fails.
- **Finding 2 (a page with no SVGs passed the preview check):** the check no longer counts path text anywhere in the HTML. It now counts real inline `<svg>` elements outside comments, scripts and templates. Each icon needs at least four, carrying its file's root stroke settings. The reviewer's comment-only page now fails.
  - M1.4 now also has a reviewer look at the page as rendered: every variant labelled, every icon at 24 and 48 px on both light and dark.
  - M2.2 now claims only what its check proves. M2.8, which already looks at the rendered page, now names all eight icons at both sizes on both panels.
- **Advisory (name icons before enlarging):** in M1.3 and M2.3 the reviewer now names each icon from the 24 px capture at its real size first. Enlarged crops are only for explaining a miss.
- **Design (`ICONS.md`):** the contract and mechanisms 5 and 6 now say these stroke and fill settings are required on the root and banned on children. They also say whether the preview draws correctly is judged by looking at the rendered page.
- **Plan:** status lines and log are updated. I didn't touch `fails` or `replans`, since this is a design revision, not a re-plan.

**Checks:**
- Both of the reviewer's counterexamples now fail, and a correct test set passes.
- With no icons yet, every item's check comes back `fail` rather than `error`, and the project-wide check passes.
- The new definitions are M1.1, M1.3, M1.4, M2.1, M2.2, M2.3 and M2.8.

This worktree's branch (`build/ICONS`) is one commit behind `main`. That commit holds the design review and the updated `ICONS-ACCEPTED.json`, so the loop needs to merge them when it integrates.

**Owner decisions:**
- No new decisions are needed.
- One stricter reading: the contract now requires exactly `width="24"`. The old checker also accepted `"24px"`, so you can widen this in a line if you want to.
- M1 still ends with you picking a drawing direction, as planned.
